_note: Narration for the calm 90-second cut (calm90), one line per feature. Record each line as its own file named by its id (title, s1 ... s10, end), then: python3 voice/import.py <folder> --edit calm90.

lines.text: This is iTalmud: the Illustrated Talmud.
Every daf comes with a study outline. Open a section to see its steps, and insights from the shiur.
At the end, a summary of the whole daf, each point linked back to its section.
Charts set the cases side by side, with an icon for every ruling.
Illustrations draw each case, and how each opinion rules on it.
Tap a key term for its definition, or a measure to see it on a scale.
Tap a sage to meet him, and explore his teachers and students.
Test yourself with a quiz on every daf. Each answer links to its place on the daf.
The outline and the Talmud move together. Tap a section, and the Gemara goes there, in Hebrew, English, or both.
On the daf page too, with the Rambam and Shulchan Arukh in the margin.
And every word opens to its meaning, and its entry in the dictionary.
The Talmud. Explicated. Annotated. Illustrated. italmud dot com.
